topic: Linear Chromosome Ends, Telomeres, & Ribonucleoprotein Telomerase
quickSummary: Linear eukaryotic chromosomes face the end-replication problem at lagging strand 5' ends upon primer removal. Telomeres (5'-TTAGGG-3' repeats in humans) protect chromosome ends. Telomerase is a specialized reverse transcriptase ribonucleoprotein carrying an internal RNA template (3'-CAAUCCCAAUC-5') that extends the 3' overhang.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Linear eukaryotic chromosomes cannot replicate the extreme 5' end of lagging strands because removal of the terminal RNA primer leaves an unfillable gap. Telomerase (TERT + TERC) is a ribonucleoprotein reverse transcriptase with an intrinsic RNA template (3'-CAAUCCCAAUC-5') that extends the 3' overhang with repetitive 5'-TTAGGG-3' telomeric repeats.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 5.1 The End-Replication Problem
- In linear eukaryotic chromosomes, DNA Polymerases require an upstream $3'\text{-OH}$ primer to synthesize DNA.
- When the terminal RNA primer on the lagging strand is removed by $5' \rightarrow 3'$ exonucleases, there is no upstream $3'\text{-OH}$ available for DNA polymerase to fill the resulting $8\text{--}12\text{ nucleotide}$ gap.
- Consequently, chromosomes progressively shorten with each cell cycle (Hayflick limit and cellular senescence).

### 5.2 Telomeres & Telomerase Ribonucleoprotein Complex
- **Telomeres**: Specialized non-coding nucleoprotein caps at the ends of linear chromosomes containing tandem hexanucleotide repeats (**$\text{5'-TTAGGG-3'}$** in vertebrates).
- **Telomerase Complex Components**:
  1. **TERC (Telomerase RNA Component)**: Serves as the internal template ($3'\text{-CAAUCCCAAUC-5'}$).
  2. **TERT (Telomerase Reverse Transcriptase)**: Catalytic protein subunit that reverse-transcribes the RNA template into DNA repeats, extending the $3'$ parental overhang.
- **Significance in Biology & Medicine**:
  - Highly active in germ cells, stem cells, and $\approx 85\text{--}90\%$ of human **cancer cells** (conferring cellular immortality), but inactive in normal somatic cells.

conceptBreakdown.heading: T-Loop and Shelterin Complex
conceptBreakdown.title: T-Loop and Shelterin Complex
conceptBreakdown.content: The single-stranded 3' telomeric G-rich overhang invades the double-stranded telomeric tract to form a protective T-loop stabilized by the 6-protein Shelterin complex (TRF1, TRF2, POT1, RAP1, TIN2, TPP1), preventing chromosome end-to-end fusions.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres (ALT)
conceptBreakdown.title: Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres (ALT)
conceptBreakdown.content: A subset (10-15%) of human cancers lack telomerase and instead maintain telomere length through homologous recombination-based Alternative Lengthening of Telomeres (ALT).
